set.approach: Drive to the Fairy Lake road, pass the Shafthouse trailhead, and park beyond the Forest Service gate beside the two well-used campsites. Pick up the narrow trail opposite the parking area, cross the creek and climb the short steep hill to the big meadow, then follow the trail nearly to the top of it, stopping short of the line of trees at the saddle. Leave the trail to the left and go through a gap in the small ridge; Arrowhead is the tallest peak in the bowl, behind the gray limestone wall. Climb the scree on the right to the apron where Arrowhead extends into the bowl. Alpine Boogie climbs the southeast face of Arrowhead, beginning from a handful of ledges that funnel into an open book, with gray rock on its right and a ramp to its left.
set.descent_text: Walk off. The last pitch ends on the summit of Arrowhead. Walk down the ridge west to the Bridger Ridge trail and follow it over the next rises in the ridge, not dropping too early, to a large saddle at the Sacajawea trail. Take that trail left down to the trailhead, then the road back to the parking area.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the area page; route page for the face and start. Distances and times left out (single source).

set.approach: Use the Arrowhead Peak approach, but do not go as far into the bowl. Drive to the Fairy Lake road, pass the Shafthouse trailhead, and park beyond the Forest Service gate beside the two well-used campsites. Pick up the narrow trail opposite the parking area, cross the creek and climb the short steep hill to the big meadow, then follow the trail nearly to the top of it, stopping short of the line of trees at the saddle. Leave the trail to the left and go through a gap in the small ridge; Arrowhead is the tallest peak in the bowl, behind the gray limestone wall. Go up the loose scree apron to the right as far as the first big gully. This is among the lowest crack systems on the east face; it begins at a broken crack set a little up from the arete, at the downhill end of the limestone wall.
set.descent_text: Above the second pitch, a walk east leads to the scree gully that lies straight above the start; descend it to the packs.

review.notes: Route page states the walk-off and start; area page gives the trail approach.

set.approach: From the sign at Ross Pass, angle left of the Shish Kabob summit to where the terrain forms a gully. There is no defined trail, so follow the path of least resistance down the gully. Routes lie on both sides of it, and Run Ross Run is on skier's left, across from Red October.

review.notes: Approach from the area page; position from the route page. No descent stated for this route.

set.approach: Take the usual No Sweat approach trail to the point beneath the ramp that gives access to the Awakening Wall and the routes on the upper rim, then work westward along faint game trails to the Gray and Pro wall area, and traverse beneath the wall to a big arete on the right of a massive rocky gully. A bolt on this arete marks the start of the first pitch.
set.descent_text: All the anchors are bolted and set up for rappelling, so the route is descended by rappelling it.

review.notes: Route page; rope length left out (single source).

set.approach: From the Beehive Basin trailhead hike up the basin to the lake. Honey Bee Wall is the obvious rock formation on the northwest side of the lake. The route is the most obvious crack on the left side of the wall.

review.notes: Approach from area page; location from the route page. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the Beehive Basin trailhead hike up the basin to the lake. Honey Bee Wall is the obvious rock formation on the northwest side of the lake. The route starts below the discontinuous crack on the right side of the wall, where a rightward-slanting ledge at the lower left gives access to the crack.

review.notes: Approach from area page; location from the route page. No descent stated.

set.approach: Log Jam Boulder is on the east side of the lake near the logs in the water, a short way south of the lake campsites. It is the largest boulder in the talus pile, and the route is on its lake-facing side.

review.notes: Area page for location; route page for the face. No descent stated.

set.approach: Log Jam Boulder is on the east side of the lake near the logs in the water, a short way south of the lake campsites. It is the largest boulder in the talus pile, and the route is on its lake-facing side.

set.approach: Follow the Lost Cabin Lake Trail until just short of the lake, then climb the talus up to the base of the buttress. The line begins to the right of the big arete's foot and mostly stays on the crest.

review.notes: Approach from the area page; start from the route page. No descent stated.

set.approach: Take the trail toward Lost Cabin Lake and leave it just short of the lake. Go up talus to the right of the trail to the obvious gray slab on the buttress, northwest of the lake.
set.descent_text: The route finishes on top of the buttress crest. The back of the formation is a walk-off that rejoins the trail.

review.notes: Route page states approach and walk-off.

set.approach: Start at the East Rosebud trailhead near Alpine and follow the trail south beyond the head of the lake, passing a rock outcrop, a stream ford, a large waterfall and a run of switchbacks. Leave the trail where a wide talus wash climbs toward the left flank of the Lower Doublet, and follow the wash through chockstones and boulders until a cliff band has been passed on the right and a vertical waterfall appears. Go right there, up a fourth-class slab, to the hillside directly below the Lower Doublet. The line takes the central prow of the Lower Doublet.
set.descent_text: The descent is by rappel down the route.

review.notes: Route page: 'rappel route'; Doublets page: approach. Distance, gain and rope count left out. Page counts 11 pitches to the junction with another route, stored as 14.

set.approach: Approach from Beehive Basin or the North Fork trailhead. The formation is an obvious prow at the end of the ridge dividing Bear and Middle basins. Go from the trail to the base through the talus, staying on the trail until some elevation has been gained rather than cutting up early. From the base keep heading south to the foot of a short lead with a clear corner crack and a two-bolt anchor visible above.
set.descent_text: Walk off to the northeast. If a rappel is needed, it goes straight down.

review.notes: Route page states approach details and descent.

set.approach: Approach from Beehive Basin or the North Fork trailhead into the North Fork drainage. The line begins in the left-hand dihedral of the formation, a start it shares with False Charge and Bear Scant, and then follows the first broken crack system upward.
set.descent_text: Walking off is possible by heading directly back from the top and finding a way down. Alternatively, rappel from the sling on the tree above the fifth-pitch variation down the route to the top of the second pitch, then to the top of the first pitch of False Charge and to the ground, with some swinging involved.

review.notes: Route page states start and both descent options; area page gives the trailheads. Rappel count left out.

set.approach: From the Granite Lake trailhead hike to the southern end of the lake and circle it to the far end, where a peninsula has a primitive campsite. Stay to climber's right of the feature called Thunderdome and follow the obvious gully and snow slope. Look for a big block that has partly pulled away from the wall, with a ramp running up on its right; the route starts at the crack where the block meets the cliff, or up the ramp.

review.notes: Approach from the route and area pages. The route page says only that several descent options exist, so no descent written.

set.approach: Follow the Gunsight Pass trail out of Lake McDonald and into the Lake Ellen Wilson basin. The central, largest buttress above the trail is Palm Springs, the second you meet coming from the west. When you draw level with it, leave the trail and climb the open beargrass slopes to the rock. The route begins close to the southern toe of the buttress, in a broad slot whose left wall is a roof-capped, right-facing corner and whose right side is a pillar.
set.descent_text: From the top, traverse climber's left and slightly up, and descend the first big gully on the left flank of the buttress. Follow it down until you can cross skier's right to a grassy series of ledges, cross the intermittent creek draining the basin, and work down the ledges to the talus. Steep snow can fill this ground, calling for an ice axe and sometimes crampons. Follow the talus down to the Gunsight Pass trail.

review.notes: Route page states start and descent; area page the approach. Distances left out.

set.approach: Follow the Gunsight Pass trail out of Lake McDonald and into the Lake Ellen Wilson basin. The central, largest buttress above the trail is Palm Springs, the second you meet coming from the west. When you draw level with it, leave the trail and climb the open beargrass slopes to the rock. Logistics Meeting begins at the extreme west end of the buttress, under a prominent right-facing corner set in a bright band of red argillite.
set.descent_text: The route ends at a grassy ledge just below the standard walk-off. Go left and down along the ledge to the creek, cross it, drop through ledges to the talus, then follow the talus to the Gunsight Pass trail. The talus can hold steep snow.

review.notes: Route page states start and descent; area page the approach.

set.approach: Follow the Gunsight Pass trail out of Lake McDonald and into the Lake Ellen Wilson basin. The central, largest buttress above the trail is Palm Springs, the second you meet coming from the west. When you draw level with it, leave the trail and climb the open beargrass slopes to the rock. Tropical Dance begins at the west side of the buttress, up on a stack of three grassy ledges entered from the climber's left. Traverse the top ledge until below the large triangular roofs; the route begins at a shallow left-facing corner.
set.descent_text: Scramble up nearly to the top of the buttress, where a run of ledges heads left. Follow them across the creek, descend the ledges to the talus, and follow the talus out to the Gunsight Pass trail. The talus can hold steep snow.

review.notes: Route page states start and descent.

set.approach: Park west of Logan Pass, then cross the basin beneath the road to the foot of the slab. Climb the talus cone that rises to the slab, keeping to its left flank. The line is a broken crack system on clean rock straight above a big boulder, which doubles as the first belay stance.
set.descent_text: From the top walk up a little, then traverse hard left back to the Oberlin climbers trail, which leads to the parking lot.

review.notes: Route page states start and descent; area page the parking. Distance and time left out.

set.approach: Hike the Sphinx Mountain trail to the saddle between Sphinx Mountain and the Helmet. From the saddle, climb the steep hillside to the left to the foot of the Helmet. The crack lies left of the prominent ramp, well downhill of the arete of the Helmet feature.
set.descent_text: At the top of the second pitch, go up the broad ledge and step out onto the steep grass slope of the Helmet. The way down is a walk-off, going through a hole in the cliff band, which sits below the slabby stretch crossed on the way down the Helmet.

review.notes: Route page; distances and times left out.

set.approach: Take the North Rim approach in Mill Creek, and once beyond the Pirate's Cove sector keep going up canyon below the cliff. This is the Upper Tier, and the White Wall is part of it. Kids with Guns opens the White Wall, reached where the path steepens past Pirate's Cove; look for a large pine toward the top of the wall and a line of bolts trending right up through the chossy roof feature.
set.descent_text: All anchors are bolted, so the route can be rappelled, or you can walk off toward the Tick Farm area.

review.notes: Route page states retreat options; Upper Tier page the approach.

set.approach: From the West Fork trailhead take the trail that passes right under the formation, which is north of the trail. Leave the trail and follow ridges and gullies through forest and meadow up the slope; granitic slabs appear in the upper section, but the path only walks beneath them. Go up the gully beneath the formation, then switch into the forest trending left where the gully narrows. Stay below the slabs and move up and left toward the descent ramp, then cross a wooded ledge into the slabs and reach the foot of the route, which climbs a clean slab into a left-to-right leaning corner.
set.descent_text: Rappel to the ledge under the summit block and downclimb into the gully; climb the gully a way, then cut left into the forest. Traverse in the forest to a big clean face next to a flowered meadow, and follow the base of the Witchtowers slabs back to your packs.

review.notes: Route page; elevations, distances and rappel details left out (single source).
